## kb_to_source
Sentence-level read of every normative claim in the 53 docs: each traces to a base rule, an extended rule, a variant parameter, the parameter_schema, the lifecycle or an eligibility/evidence contract. No added confirmation, review, notification, wait or step. Specific checks:
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call ..."): none. Each task-tool name appears only in its own policy's invocation block (regex over all docs).
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none (all examples marked hypothetical; no task's customer, dates or amounts appear).
- Interpretive glosses checked and found entailed by the source: "Request: ... the most recently submitted one where there are several" (baseline docs; source compute LATEST by submitted_date); "A payable is never below zero" in the DM baseline doc (source assembly "never below zero"); "The size test is made on that gross" (compute uses gross).
- Additions: none. Omissions: none. Rewrites: none.
- Policy-side note (not a KB verdict): `check_and_unclaimed_terms_schedule` renders the parameter_schema descriptions of `check_reissue_free_count` ("reissues of one payout made free of charge") and `check_reissue_fee` ("fee deducted from a reissued check beyond the free reissues") and explains "One reissue of a payout is made without charge; the $15.00 fee is the fee deducted from a reissued check beyond the free reissue". That per-payout semantics belongs to the clause the overwrite retired; the schema descriptions were not updated with the overwrite, so the KB faithfully carries a source-layer tension (the current rule counts voids on the account and has a $25.00 tier). It is outside this task's computations. Similarly, base `capital_evt_early_retirement` keeps "may ask for all of the account's unretired credits" in force while the overwrite limits the booking to DM rows; the KB carries both as the source does.
